metadata.research_goal: Deepen boxing punch mechanics for jab, cross, hooks, uppercuts, body shots, and combinations with coaching cues, errors, progression, and injury risk.

key_concepts.summary: Punching quality depends on stance, foot pressure, hip/trunk transfer, shoulder control, and guard return.
Jab and cross control long range, entries, counters, and scoring rhythm.
Hooks and uppercuts require range, elbow/wrist structure, and hip rotation.
Body punching should lower through knees and hips, not by folding at the waist.
Combinations should have target, tempo, defense, and exit logic, not random punch strings.
High-volume bag work should stop or regress when form breaks.

technical_models.mechanics: Lead-hand straight punch; elbow drives through target; retracts on same line.
technical_models.progression: static jab -> step jab -> double/body jab -> jab-entry-exit

technical_models.mechanics: Rear straight punch; rear-to-lead weight shift; toe-hip-shoulder rotation.
technical_models.progression: rear straight -> jab-cross -> body/head cross -> cross after slip/parry

technical_models.mechanics: Bent-arm rotational punch; pivot hips/shoulders; elbow near 90 degrees.
technical_models.progression: lead hook form -> bag 50 percent -> head/body hook -> hook after roll/slip

technical_models.mechanics: Short rising rotational punch; bend knees, load hip, keep elbow bent.
technical_models.progression: short uppercut -> close mitt/bag -> hook-uppercut -> counter uppercut inside

technical_models.mechanics: Straight, hook, or uppercut to torso above belt; lower through knees, eyes up.
technical_models.progression: target-line drill -> body jab/cross -> head-body-head -> body shot angle exit

technical_models.mechanics: Start with 2-3 punch chains; alternate hands/levels; keep stance between shots.

tactical_rules.rule: Use jab to control range, score, interrupt rhythm, and create entries.
Do not progress rear-hand power before the boxer can rotate without falling forward.
Teach hooks short and structurally sound before power or fatigue volume.
Uppercuts require correct range or space creation; long scooping uppercuts are risky.
Body shots should include head position and exit/counter responsibility.
Every combination should finish with guard return plus defense, angle, or reset.
Train speed and power before heavy fatigue work.

physical_demands.quality: Jab and guard volume demand lead shoulder endurance.
Crosses, hooks, and uppercuts need hip/trunk rotation and force transfer.
Impact punches require wrist alignment, hand wrapping, and progressive exposure.
Rear-hand and body shots need foot pressure, hip drive, and stance stability.
Combinations require repeat explosive output plus aerobic recovery.
High punch volume needs scapular control and guard-return endurance.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Poor wrist alignment on bag or pads can irritate wrist/hand structures.
High punch volume can overload shoulder and scapular control.
Over-rotation or scooping uppercuts can irritate the low back.
Poor body-shot level change can expose the head.
Fatigue can create guard drops, hand drift, and unsafe punch paths.

training_implications.summary: Database should store punch IDs separately from combinations so sessions can reference exact technique.
Power should progress from shadow to pads/bag to partner context with pain monitoring.
Combinations should include range, target, defense, exit, and fatigue context.
Hand, wrist, elbow, shoulder, or back pain should modify impact volume.
Punch drills should be taggable by round purpose: skill, power, pace, defense, or tactical scenario.
